title: A pavilion that follows the ground
summary: Raise the land under a Japanese garden pavilion. Four independent feet adapt while its deck stays level, using one editable recipe and shared terrain operators.
prompt:
Create a Japanese garden pavilion that adapts to Polynite's infinite terrain.

- Check commands.recipe_terrain, then discover architecture.operators for spatial queries.
- Compose an assembly recipe with context:[{name:'ground',terrain:'infinite'}]. Sample four feet with height; keep the deck above their maximum plus floor_clearance.
- Choose dimensions in the recipe: an unbounded terrain has no footprint width or depth.
- Expose width, depth, roof curl and floor_clearance. Raise a broad patch of ground, then return it to the initial state in a five-second film.
- Keep the existing user scene and use stable IDs. Verify the contacts visually.
try: Set floor_clearance to 0.6 under Scene settings > Living architecture > temple.
Change width, depth, curl and overhang. The same support expressions still fit the feet.
Change the raise cue depth from 4 to 2.2. Keep the ground edit broad enough for the terrain grid.
steps: Declare the support as a named context reference.
Sample its top height at four corners and choose their maximum.
Place the deck above that height; extend each foot to its own sample.
settings: Scene settings > Living architecture > temple: floor_clearance, width, depth, curl, overhang. Adjust also exposes the scene-owned Ground height control.
limits: Requires commands.recipe_terrain. Press Play to compare flat and raised ground; use Adjust for the saved controls. Terrain queries use the finest near-field triangle grid, currently 4 m. Arbitrary imported meshes and continuous terrain deformation are outside this example.
